base_sha_note: origin/main at INTEG-10 close; repo-head links below are delta baselines, not static truth — re-audit latest main before citing as current.
source_scope: Repository-native catalog tying reverse-mathematics / computability / solver / provenance priors to concrete repo applications, assumptions, falsifiers, and derivative experiment keys. Deduplicates citations and records what each source does not prove before entries may enter experiment manifests.

sources.title: Subsystems of Second Order Arithmetic
sources.claim_supported: Classical reverse mathematics organizes theorems by the second-order comprehension/choice axioms needed over a weak base theory (RCA0 and the Big Five).
does_not_prove: That any OpenUI / TwoTower empirical result is RCA0/WKL0/ACA0-equivalent
That #print axioms or Lean compile success yields a genuine RM label
That a finite fixture analogue is an interpretation package
sources.repo_relevance: Vocabulary and anti-overclaim ceiling for HARN-05/08 and KERN-12 rm_research:* labels.
sources.repo_application: Use as primary citation when defining base_theory_id / Big-Five naming; never as automatic promotion evidence.
sources.assumption: Interpretation packages must supply coding + both-direction evidence before reversed_equivalent.
sources.falsifier: Any automatic upgrade from practical_computability_only or finite analogue to Big-Five equivalence without interpretation_package evidence.

delta_baseline.note: Repo-head RM policy is a delta over Simpson; re-audit main before treating local labels as SOSOA claims.

sources.title: Constructive Reverse Mathematics: An Introduction
sources.claim_supported: Constructive reverse mathematics studies which constructive principles are needed for theorems, distinct from classical Big-Five reverse mathematics.
does_not_prove: That constructivization modes in this repo are faithful CRM theorems
That bounded_finite_analogue equals a constructive equivalence
Classical RCA0/WKL0 labels from constructive weakenings alone
sources.repo_relevance: Prior for HARN-06 constructivization modes and documented_nonconstructive_remainder.
sources.repo_application: Cite when recording weakening_description / constructivized_statement_sha256; keep classical and constructive claims separate.
sources.assumption: Every constructivized claim is a distinct proposition with an explicit weakening.
sources.falsifier: Masquerading a finite analogue or classical existence as the original constructive theorem.

delta_baseline.note: HARN-06 owners are repo deltas; re-check main before equating modes to CRM literature.

sources.title: The Reverse Mathematics Zoo: A Survey
sources.claim_supported: Surveys the Reverse Mathematics Zoo: many principles sit strictly between or outside the classical Big Five, with careful reducibility relations.
does_not_prove: That repo task ids map onto Zoo principles
Completeness of any local principle inventory
Automatic Zoo membership from naming similarity
sources.repo_relevance: Context for not collapsing every RM-inspired experiment into Big-Five labels.
sources.repo_application: Cite when arguing a principle may be intermediate / incomparable; prefer unclassified until coded.
sources.assumption: Local principle ids are hypotheses until an interpretation package exists.
sources.falsifier: Treating Zoo survey citations as certificates that a harness principle equals a named Zoo entry.

delta_baseline.note: KERN-12 vocabulary is a repo delta; Zoo citations do not enlarge the production label set.

sources.title: Mathlib Computability.Partrec — Partial Recursive Functions
sources.claim_supported: mathlib formalizes partial recursive functions and related computability notions as Lean definitions and theorems.
does_not_prove: That LeverProofLean mirrors mathlib Partrec API
That a Lean compile of a fixture implies Partrec membership
Production ship gates from mathlib presence alone
sources.repo_relevance: Lean/tooling prior for computability vocabulary and future formal bridges.
sources.repo_application: Cite when comparing repo Lean computability labels to mathlib; do not import mathlib as a silent dependency of ship gates.
sources.assumption: Any mathlib bridge is an explicit experiment with pinned revisions.
sources.falsifier: Claiming repo total_recursive / primitive_recursive labels are mathlib theorems without a checked bridge artifact.

delta_baseline.note: Local Lean inductives are delta baselines vs mathlib; re-audit docs URL and API on main.

sources.title: Bounded Arithmetic, Proof Complexity and Feasible Reasoning
sources.claim_supported: Bounded arithmetic and proof complexity connect feasible reasoning strength to resource-bounded proof systems.
does_not_prove: That MAX_RUN_MINUTES or wall-time caps are bounded-arithmetic theorems
Complexity class separations for OpenUI decode
That EG_params LCB is a proof-complexity measure
sources.repo_relevance: Literature prior for feasible / resource-bounded reasoning narratives around formal and decode budgets.
sources.repo_application: Cite when motivating bounded search / resource witnesses; keep separate from empirical latency gates.
sources.assumption: Repo cost axes remain measured engineering budgets unless a formal reduction is certified.
sources.falsifier: Equating a timed-out run with a complexity lower bound.

delta_baseline.note: Practical computability classes are repo deltas; Buss is not their soundness proof.

sources.title: Verified Complexity Reductions in Lean
sources.claim_supported: Complexity reductions can be stated and machine-checked in Lean so that claimed reductions carry formal certificates.
does_not_prove: That any current LeverProofLean object is a verified complexity reduction
Ship readiness from citing this paper
Automatic transfer of external Lean proofs into repo evidence envelopes
sources.repo_relevance: Lean/tooling prior for future certified reductions between local computability claims.
sources.repo_application: Cite when proposing reduction experiments; require content-addressed formal objects before promotion.
sources.assumption: Reductions are experiments until bound to ExperimentCampaignV1 + formal evidence.
sources.falsifier: Promotion of a reduction claim without a checked Lean/formal artifact hash.

delta_baseline.note: Formal-object owners on main are the delta baseline for any reduction pilot.

sources.title: Proof Mining and Quantitative Extraction
sources.claim_supported: Proof mining extracts quantitative bounds and computational content from (often non-constructive) proofs.
does_not_prove: That repo telemetry or NLL numbers are proof-mined bounds
Automatic extraction pipelines for OpenUI theorems
That finite_search_bound evidence is a Kohlenbach-style extract
sources.repo_relevance: Prior for quantitative witnesses and bound.* AST placeholders in constructivization.
sources.repo_application: Cite when arguing for explicit numerical bounds on search/closure; require replayable witnesses.
sources.assumption: Extracted bounds must be independently checkable artifacts, not narrative.
sources.falsifier: Calling a heuristic hyperparameter a proof-mined modulus.

delta_baseline.note: bound.* / witness owners on main are deltas; re-audit before claiming mining fidelity.

sources.title: Weihrauch Complexity and Related Topics: A Survey
sources.claim_supported: Weihrauch reducibility compares multi-valued computational problems uniformly, finer than many classical computability reductions.
does_not_prove: That any repo harness task is Weihrauch-equivalent to a named problem
Big-Five RM labels from Weihrauch degrees
That oracle_relative practical labels are Weihrauch degrees
sources.repo_relevance: Uniform reduction vocabulary for comparing problem strengths without overclaiming RM equivalence.
sources.repo_application: Cite for default-off experiments on problem reducibility; keep separate from HARN-08 Big-Five packages.
sources.assumption: Named Weihrauch degrees require explicit problem representations and reductions.
sources.falsifier: Using Weihrauch citations to justify RCA0/WKL0 production labels.

delta_baseline.note: Practical classes on main are not Weihrauch degrees; treat as delta baseline only.

sources.title: LRAT-Catcher
sources.claim_supported: LRAT-oriented tooling supports checking/catching SAT proof certificates in the LRAT family.
does_not_prove: That the repo ships an LRAT checker as a production dependency
Unsat certificates for OpenUI grammar obligations
That missing LRAT tools refute a semantic claim (timeouts stay unknown)
sources.repo_relevance: Solver/certificate standard prior for optional external proof checking experiments.
sources.repo_application: Cite in default-off formal pilots; external solvers remain experiments per revmath ADR.
sources.assumption: Certificate formats are opt-in; absence maps to unknown/inconclusive.
sources.falsifier: Treating solver absence or timeout as semantic refutation.

delta_baseline.note: Pilot format names on main are deltas; re-check before claiming LRAT integration.

sources.title: PBLean
sources.claim_supported: PBLean-style tooling targets pseudo-Boolean / related proof certificates in a Lean-adjacent workflow.
does_not_prove: Production PB certificate checking in this repo
That VSS or formal objects are PBLean certificates
Ship gates from PBLean citation
sources.repo_relevance: Solver/certificate prior for optional multi-prover certificate experiments.
sources.repo_application: Cite only for explicit default-off certificate pilots with content-addressed artifacts.
sources.assumption: Certificate backends are swappable experiments, not merge prerequisites.
sources.falsifier: Making PBLean a hard dependency of verify_merge_ready or ship gates.

delta_baseline.note: Multi-prover pilots on main are delta baselines for any PBLean experiment.

sources.title: SZS Ontologies for Automated Theorem Proving
sources.claim_supported: SZS status values standardize reporting of ATP outcomes (Theorem, Unsatisfiable, Timeout, GaveUp, …).
does_not_prove: Semantic truth of a repo claim from an SZS string alone
That Timeout/GaveUp are refutations
Equivalence between SZS and ExperimentCampaignV1 gate outcomes without a mapping table
sources.repo_relevance: Solver reporting ontology for mapping external prover exits to unknown vs success/fail.
sources.repo_application: Cite when normalizing external solver status into evidence envelopes; map Timeout→unknown.
sources.assumption: Only Success-class SZS values may support positive formal claims after independent checks.
sources.falsifier: Recording GaveUp/Timeout as counterexample_known or reversed_equivalent.

delta_baseline.note: Repo unknown/inconclusive policy is a delta overlay on SZS; re-audit mapping on main.

sources.title: LeanDojo
sources.claim_supported: LeanDojo provides data, tools, and benchmarks for learning-based theorem proving in Lean.
does_not_prove: That repo agents must call LeanDojo
Proof search success implies RM interpretation
Dataset contamination / decontamination properties for OpenUI evals
sources.repo_relevance: Lean/tooling prior for optional ML-for-theorem-proving experiments.
sources.repo_application: Cite for default-off tooling spikes; keep outside production decode and ship paths.
sources.assumption: Any LeanDojo integration is an experiment with pinned data snapshots.
sources.falsifier: Wiring LeanDojo into production constrained decode or ship gates.

delta_baseline.note: Repo-head ADR delta baseline marks external solvers/tools as experiments; LeanDojo stays in that bucket on main.

sources.title: Lean Refactor
sources.claim_supported: Automated Lean refactoring / maintenance tooling can assist large formal libraries.
does_not_prove: Correctness of LeverProofLean refactors without lake build + guards
That refactor success preserves semantic evidence hashes
License to weaken formal evidence mutation gates

sources.repo_application: Cite when proposing assisted Lean refactors; require verify_formal_* and lake build.
sources.assumption: Refactors are behavior-preserving only when formal mutation gates stay green.
sources.falsifier: Landing Lean refactors that skip formal evidence mutation checks.

delta_baseline.note: Formal mutation gate on main is the delta baseline for any refactor tool claim.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology (W3C Recommendation)
sources.claim_supported: PROV-O defines a standard OWL ontology for provenance entities, activities, and agents.
does_not_prove: That current version_stamp / lineage records are PROV-O instances
Interoperability with external PROV stores without an explicit mapping
Model quality or ship readiness from provenance markup alone

sources.assumption: Repo lineage schemas remain authoritative; PROV-O is an interchange target.
sources.falsifier: Replacing version_stamp or EvidenceCampaign contracts with ad-hoc PROV JSON without a mapping doc.

delta_baseline.note: version_stamp on main is the delta baseline; PROV-O does not supersede it.

Training-data legality from SPDX fields alone

External solver availability

sources.title: Explicit repository-only hypothesis (no external prior)

That the hypothesis is true
Exemption from ExperimentCampaignV1 or ship-gate honesty
